phases.objective: Move the unchanged Hostinger workflow_run publisher to a canonical workflow path so GitHub registers the specialized publisher without changing its permissions, artifact identity, PR resolution, comment authority, or runtime safety boundary.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: The specialized Hostinger publisher workflow and its static contract test
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Exactly one specialized publisher workflow remains at the canonical path and retains the existing workflow_run trigger, trusted-main checkout, run-bound artifact download, and bounded authoritative-comment update contract.
steps: Register the byte-equivalent publisher at the canonical workflow path.
Remove the previous workflow path to prevent duplicate workflow_run publishers.
Update the static contract test and E2E evidence paths to the canonical path.
Run the specialized publisher normalization and comment-upsert regression suite.
assertions: The workflow name remains Hostinger CI Evidence PR Publisher.
The trigger remains workflow_run completed for Hostinger Storage Tenant Canary Guard only.
Permissions remain actions:read, contents:read, issues:write, and pull-requests:write.
The publisher checks out trusted main with persist-credentials:false.
No PR-head code receives comment-write authority.
No provider, credential, SQL, migration, deployment, Production, protected-branch, or force-push action occurs.

phases.objective: After merge, complete a new exact-head Tenant Canary run and prove the re-registered publisher writes the Hostinger section to the shared authoritative PR comment.
blockers: The canonical publisher path has not reached main yet.
No post-registration workflow_run publication has been observed.

phases.objective: Prove idempotent publisher retries and rejection of stale, ambiguous, malformed, missing-artifact, and mismatched-workflow evidence.
This change registers a repository evidence publisher and does not execute a live Hostinger canary.
The publisher grants no runtime, deployment, migration, provider, or Production authority.
